value.title: Fifer: Practical Acceleration of Irregular Applications on Reconfigurable Architectures
value.locator_basis: 1-based cached proceedings PDF pages; printed page numbers1-14

value.statement: Programs are manually partitioned to decouple irregular memory operations; LLVM IR regular stages are mapped through DFGs and generated bitstreams. Queue control values delineate stage control boundaries.
limitations: Paper architecture scope only; exact RTL, compiled stage configurations and memory/queue ABI require implementation binding.

value.statement: New configuration loads into inactive double-buffered cells while the active fabric stops accepting inputs and drains in-flight operations. Activation follows both completion conditions. Required stage state is drained to L1 for preservation; the evaluated activation dead time is two cycles.
limitations: Paper architecture scope only; exact RTL, compiled stage configurations and memory/queue ABI require implementation binding.

value.statement: A PE retains its current stage until input empty or output full. The next stage is selected among unblocked stages according to greatest work available in input queues; no detailed tie-breaking policy is supplied.
limitations: Paper architecture scope only; exact RTL, compiled stage configurations and memory/queue ABI require implementation binding.

value.statement: Each PE has statically partitioned circular queue storage in a16KB SRAM reference. Additional head/tail pointers support intra-PE stage queues alongside inter-PE queues. This is distinct from Pipette physical-register-file queue storage.
limitations: Paper architecture scope only; exact RTL, compiled stage configurations and memory/queue ABI require implementation binding.

value.statement: DRMs receive address operands for dereference or address-range pairs for sequential scanning. Their accesses can complete out of order, but an available result waits for earlier accesses before output enqueue. DRMs are configured at initialization and keep operating independently of the scheduled fabric stage.
limitations: Paper architecture scope only; exact RTL, compiled stage configurations and memory/queue ABI require implementation binding.

value.statement: An additional control bit travels in queues and through functional units, preserving order boundaries. Data-parallel stage replicas can dequeue multiple data values together; control values are handled one per cycle. Spatial partitioning sends owned work to another PE instead of shared-memory synchronization.
limitations: Paper architecture scope only; exact RTL, compiled stage configurations and memory/queue ABI require implementation binding.

value.description: Regular CGRA stages time-multiplexed by queue readiness with independent FIFO-return DRMs; no operation inheritance from Pipette.

value.name: Fifer MICRO2021 temporal CGRA stages with DRMs
value.summary: Queue-ready temporal stage scheduling with double-buffered reconfiguration and independent in-order DRM result delivery.

interface.software_supplies: Manually partitioned regular stages, compiled DFG/bitstream configurations, queue partition/connections and initial DRM dereference/scan configuration.
interface.invocation: Runtime PE scheduler retains unblocked stage, selects queue-ready work, drains fabric while loading inactive configuration, then activates it. Stages enqueue DRM address/range operands.
interface.outputs: Queue-delivered load values and control tokens; fabric state preserved across stage changes.

realization.description: Explicit stage-generated addresses enter the initialization-bound DRM input FIFO; loaded values return in request order to the next-stage queue.

result.form: Loaded opaque values in the configured DRM output FIFO.
result.validity: Explicit staged program mapping, initial DRM configuration and queue/storage/memory ownership; no CPU-register or generic gather ABI inferred.

ordering.description: Memory responses may complete out of order. Result enqueue waits for earlier accesses; queue control tokens retain sequence boundaries. No global ordering across DRMs/PEs is inferred.

completion.event: Returned value becomes available in output queue after earlier requests complete.
completion.visibility: Stage/FIFO availability does not certify host-visible program completion or store fences; concrete integration must bind those separately.

requirements.description: Bind actual stage partition, LLVM/DFG mapping and compiled fabric state; scalar code or Pipette queue tokens cannot substitute.
Declare per-stage/DRM endpoints, statically allocated queue capacities, head/tail state, backpressure and control/data encoding.
Stop accepting active-stage inputs and finish in-flight fabric operations; preserve final old state and complete new configuration before activation.
Bind every outstanding request to its original DRM/output stream; completion out of order must not reorder consumer result delivery. Fabric switches must not reassign pending DRM results.
Preserve per-stage/PE data ownership and control boundaries. Physical memory translation, permissions and queue routes require actual implementation proof.
Authenticate exact memory/queue ABI, datatype/width, protection/coherence, faults and host-visible completion.

parameters.notes: Reference total statically divided among queues; not per-queue capacity or inferred PRF ownership.
Activation dead time only, excludes variable fabric drain/configuration loads; not measured by this helper.
Explicit actual capacity must be bound before issuing requests.

internal_mechanisms.description: Statically partitioned intra/inter-PE queues persist while stages switch; distinct from Pipette PRF queues.
Active/inactive configuration cells overlap load with drain; final old stage state is preserved through L1.
Retain current unblocked stage; choose unblocked stage with greatest available input work when blocked.
Fabric drain gates activation; initialization-bound DRMs may remain outstanding independent of scheduled stage.
Out-of-order memory completion is restored to request order before DRM result enqueue.
Control bit travels in order with data; serial control-token handling establishes local phase boundaries.
Result is delivered only when available and earlier requests have completed. No global host-visible fence is supplied.

limitations: Abstract tested single-input/single-output stage lifecycle is not compiled CGRA execution, RTL or measured timing.
Exact memory-result buffer, queue word width and protection/atomic/fence ABI unknown.
Most-work tie-breaking and multichannel readiness arbitration not established.
No inherited Pipette queue-register capacity, general gather or BFS acceptance.
